name: Hazel on the Operating Table
description: Hazel lies on the operating table, undergoing surgery. The room is tense, the air heavy. It is a nightmare.
related_events: Hazel undergoes surgery on the operating table

name: Hazel Calls Him Back Under the Stars
description: Hazel lies on the grass in her backyard, gazing up at the night sky. The stars spread across the darkness above her. She takes out her phone and dials, waiting as the call connects.
related_events: Hazel lies on the grass stargazing in her backyard
Hazel calls him back while lying on the grass

name: Hazel's Biopsy and Diagnosis Disclosure
description: Hazel lies still during a biopsy procedure in a clinical room. A doctor performs the test, extracting tissue for analysis. Later, in the same setting, Hazel speaks directly to the camera, her voice steady. She says she has been diagnosed with stage IV thyroid cancer.
related_events: Hazel undergoes a biopsy procedure
Hazel reveals her stage IV thyroid cancer diagnosis

name: Hazel Returns Home Looking Distressed
description: Hazel's parents bring her home from the hospital. When they arrive, Hazel looks miserable. She shows clear signs of distress, her mood heavy and withdrawn.
related_events: Hazel's parents bring her home from the hospital
Hazel appears visibly distressed after returning home

name: Hazel Avoids Gus's Call and Withdraws to Her Room
description: Hazel sits staring into space as the house phone rings. Michael enters from another room, holding the phone. He whispers, 'Gus again.' Hazel pauses, then silently shakes her head. Michael speaks into the phone, 'I'm sorry, Gus, she's asleep.' Hazel stands and walks into her bedroom, closing the door behind her.
related_events: Hazel silently refuses to speak to Gus
Michael answers the house phone and speaks to Gus
Hazel retreats to her bedroom showing signs of depression

name: Hazel Undergoes a Medical Imaging Scan
description: Hazel lies on a narrow table in a hospital gown as the technician positions her for the scan. The machine hums softly, its wide ring looming overhead. The technician reminds her to stay still and try to relax. Hazel closes her eyes, breathes evenly, and waits. The table slides forward, carrying her slowly into the machine. Inside, the space is tight and cool. She does not move.
related_events: Hazel undergoes medical imaging procedure
Technician provides instructions during medical procedure

name: Hazel Argues with Parents About Going to Support Group
description: Hazel stands in the kitchen with her parents, refusing to go to support group. She grimaces and says they can't make her attend. Michael insists they can, reminding her they are her parents. He tells her she needs to leave the house and make friends, to be a teenager. Hazel replies that if they want her to be a teenager, they should buy her a fake ID so she can go to clubs, drink gimlets, and smoke pot. Michael points out she doesn’t even smoke pot. Hazel says that’s exactly the kind of thing she’d know if she had a fake ID. Frannie, after a pause, tells her to get in the car. Hazel responds by pretending to stab herself in the stomach with an invisible sword.
related_events: Hazel refuses to attend support group
Michael insists Hazel must attend support group
Frannie commands Hazel to get in the car

name: Michael Brings Hazel to the Emergency Room
description: Michael carries Hazel into the emergency room, moving quickly through the chaos. She is crying and in distress. Doctors immediately surround them, rushing to help. Hazel is taken from Michael and wheeled away on a gurney, leaving her family behind as medical staff move fast around her.
related_events: Michael carries Hazel into the emergency room
Doctors rally to assist the crying child
Hazel is wheeled away from her family

name: Gus Calls Hazel During Isaac's Breakdown
description: Isaac lies on Gus's couch, sobbing uncontrollably, his face buried in the cushions. Gus crouches beside him, speaking urgently into his phone. Through the line, Hazel hears muffled wails but cannot make sense of what is happening. Gus shifts his attention between Isaac and the call, trying to steady both. He tells Isaac to focus, to look at him, then turns back to the phone. After a pause, he asks Hazel how quickly she can get to his apartment. She hesitates, listening to the sounds in the background, then looks up, making a decision.
related_events: Isaac has a nervous breakdown on Gus's couch
Gus talks to Hazel on the phone while managing Isaac's crisis
Hazel hears Isaac's wailing and becomes confused
Gus asks Hazel to come over urgently

name: Frannie Waits for Hazel After the Meeting
description: Frannie sits in the car, reading a book while parked outside the church. The church door opens, and she closes her book, setting it aside. Hazel steps out, pauses, and walks over to the car. Without speaking, she gets inside. Frannie looks at her, waiting, but Hazel only exhales quietly as she settles into the seat.
related_events: Frannie waits in car while reading book
Church door opens signaling end of group session
Frannie puts away book upon seeing church door open
Hazel exits church and reacts silently to Frannie's unspoken question

name: Hazel Recovers in the Hospital Room
description: The sun shines through the window into the room. Hazel, 14 years old, slowly eats ice chips. Color returns to her cheeks. The antibiotics begin to work. Doctors drain fluid from her lungs. Over time, she grows stronger.
related_events: Antibiotics take effect in Hazel's treatment
Fluid is drained from Hazel's lungs
Hazel recovers and gains strength over time
Hazel consumes ice chips as her health improves

name: Hazel Ignores Gus's Text After Bedtime
description: Her parents tuck her in and tell her they’ll be right outside. Hazel nods. Her phone buzzes. She looks at the screen and sees a text from Gus that reads: 'ok?' She stares at the message, then puts the phone down without replying.
related_events: Hazel receives text message from Gus
Hazel decides not to respond to Gus's message

name: Parents Tuck Hazel into Bed
description: Hazel's parents tuck her into bed. They tell her they'll be right outside. Hazel nods. Her phone buzzes with a text from Gus that says: 'ok?' She looks at the message but does not reply.
related_events: Parents tuck Hazel into bed

name: Hazel and Frannie Disagree About the Donation
description: Frannie folds laundry as Hazel pleads with her to accept a donation from a man they don’t know well. Frannie resists, saying it feels wrong to take something so significant from someone who’s essentially a stranger. Hazel insists the man isn’t a stranger and objects to Frannie’s characterization. When Frannie still refuses, Hazel suggests they ask Dr. Maria for her opinion, hoping another perspective might help.
related_events: Hazel pleads her case to Frannie while laundry is folded
Frannie refuses Hazel's request due to donor's unfamiliarity
Hazel argues that the donor is not a stranger
Hazel proposes seeking Dr. Maria's opinion

name: Michael Drives, Frannie Comforts Hazel, Hazel Suffers Silently
description: Michael drives the car, his hands steady on the wheel despite the tension in his face. In the back seat, Frannie cradles Hazel’s head in her lap, one hand gently resting on her forehead. Hazel does not make a sound, but her body tenses and her mouth opens in a silent scream. Her eyes are wide, unblinking, fixed on the ceiling of the car. Outside, the road stretches forward under gray sky. A voice, Hazel’s, speaks quietly, almost detached: 'I'd been poked and stabbed and poisoned for years and still I trod on.'
related_events: Hazel silently screams in distress
Frannie comforts Hazel in the back seat
Michael drives while struggling to maintain composure
Hazel reflects on enduring prolonged medical suffering

name: Hazel's Nighttime Scream
description: Hazel wakes suddenly, screaming and clutching her head. Frannie and Michael rush into her room. Frannie takes Hazel in her arms, holding her tightly while gesturing to Michael to call for help. Michael leaves the room, and Frannie remains, rocking Hazel back and forth, whispering that everything will be okay.
related_events: Hazel wakes up screaming and clutching her head
Frannie and Michael rush into Hazel's room
Mom comforts Hazel while signaling Michael to call for help
Michael leaves the room to call for help
Frannie stays behind rocking Hazel and offering reassurance

name: Hazel Looks in the Mirror
description: Hazel catches her breath, steadying herself after a sudden emotional moment. She turns to the mirror and looks at her reflection. Her expression darkens, her face tightening with discomfort. The Earth begins to move again.
related_events: Hazel catches her breath and composes herself
Hazel looks in the mirror and reacts negatively

name: The Earth Begins to Move Again
description: After a stillness that halts everything, the Earth slowly starts turning once more. The ground trembles faintly beneath Hazel’s feet. She looks up from the mirror, breath caught in her throat, and the world around her stirs back to motion.
related_events: Earth resumes movement after a pause

name: Hazel's Parents Stay by Her Side Before Surgery
description: Hazel lies in the hospital bed, her mother Frannie standing over her, holding her hand. Frannie asks through tears if she is ready. Hazel nods. Her father stands nearby, weeping, and leans into Frannie’s shoulder. The doctors begin administering the anaesthetic. Hazel’s eyes grow heavy, her breathing slows, and she loses consciousness.
related_events: Hazel's parents stay by her side before medical procedure
Doctors administer anaesthetic to Hazel

name: Hazel Hears Her Mother's Words
description: As the anaesthetic takes hold, Hazel begins to lose consciousness. Her mother, Frannie, stands by her side, holding her hand. Hazel hears Frannie say, 'I won't be a mom anymore,' through her tears. Frannie turns and collapses into her husband's chest. Hazel fades out, the words lingering in her mind.
related_events: Hazel hears her mother's emotional statement during anaesthetic

name: Hazel Calls Gus and Starts Reading
description: Hazel sits down on a patio chair and dials the phone. Gus answers on the first ring. Hazel begins, 'Welcome to the sweet torture of reading "An Imperial --"' when she is interrupted by a loud wail from the other end of the line. 'What the -- are you ok?' she asks. Gus replies, 'Me? Yeah. I'm excellent.'
related_events: Hazel dials the phone and begins reading to Gus
Gus answers the phone and responds to Hazel

name: Hazel Hears a Wail During the Call
description: Hazel sits on a patio chair, phone in hand, speaking to Gus. As she begins to say, 'Welcome to the sweet torture of reading "An Imperial --"', a loud wail erupts from the other end of the line. She stops mid-sentence, startled. 'What the -- are you ok?' she asks. Gus replies, 'Me? Yeah. I'm excellent.'
related_events: Loud wail interrupts the phone conversation

name: Hazel Shares Her Health and GED News During Car Ride to Gus's House
description: Gus drives Hazel to his house, one eye on the road and the other on her. Hazel tells him that her tumors have shrunk and her metastases have barely grown, though her lungs still don't work well. Gus is impressed and says, 'Wow.' Hazel nods. He asks if she’s back in school, and she says she can’t go because she already earned her GED. Gus smiles and calls her a college girl, teasing her about her sophistication. Hazel laughs and playfully shoves his upper arm. They keep smiling at each other as Gus pulls the car into his driveway, parking just as awkwardly as he drives.
related_events: Hazel reveals her tumor stability and ongoing lung issues
Gus drives Hazel to his house while engaging in meaningful conversation
Gus expresses admiration for Hazel's sophistication after learning she has her GED
Hazel playfully shoves Gus during their conversation

name: Gus Parks the Car at Home
description: Gus steers the car into his driveway and brings it to a stop. The engine quiets. He handles the car with the same calm focus he maintained throughout the drive, despite his awkward parking maneuver. The ride is over. They sit for a moment in the stillness of the parked car.
related_events: Gus successfully parks his car in his driveway at the end of the drive

name: Hazel Has Dinner with Her Parents After Hearing About the PET Scan
description: Hazel sits at the table with her parents, eating dinner. Frannie mentions that Dr. Maria called and scheduled the PET scan for the eighth. Hazel nods, but doesn’t dwell on it. She continues eating, and her parents exchange a quiet look, noticing she’s eating more than usual. Frannie says she told Michael that Support Group was a good idea. Hazel’s phone buzzes. She glances at the screen. ‘Augustus,’ she says, looking up at her parents. Michael gestures toward the phone. ‘By all means.’
related_events: Frannie informs Hazel about the PET scan appointment
Hazel has dinner with her parents

name: Hazel Receives a Text from Augustus at Dinner
description: Hazel is having dinner with her parents when her phone buzzes. She sees the message and says, 'Augustus.' She looks to her parents. Michael nods and says, 'By all means.' Hazel picks up her phone and begins to respond.
related_events: Hazel receives a text message from Augustus

name: Hazel Undergoes Phalanxifor Treatment
description: Hazel began receiving intravenous medication as part of the experimental Phalanxifor trial, a treatment known for its low success rate. After completing the regimen, she underwent imaging to assess her condition. A second radiologist reviewed the follow-up X-ray and registered a visible sign of surprise. The scans showed clear improvement—her condition had responded to the treatment in a way that defied expectations.
related_events: Hazel receives intravenous medication
Hazel enrolls in experimental Phalanxifor trial
Radiologist examines second X-ray
Phalanxifor treatment shows unexpected success in Hazel

name: The Medical Team Declares Hazel's Recovery a Miracle
description: After Hazel showed significant improvement following the Phalanxifor treatment, the medical team reviewed her results. A second radiologist examined a new X-ray and appeared surprised. The doctors gathered and officially referred to her recovery as 'The Miracle.' Hazel, hearing the news, reflected on how the treatment had failed in most patients but had somehow worked for her.
related_events: Medical team dubs Hazel's recovery a miracle

name: Hazel Endures Gus's Bumpy Ride
description:
Hazel clutches the seat as Gus slams on the brakes, her body jerking forward against the seatbelt. Seconds later, he accelerates hard, snapping her head back. She stares at him, wide-eyed. Gus admits he failed his driving test a few times. Hazel mutters a dry remark under her breath. He explains that most amputees drive fine, but he’s an exception. She says she’s surprised he has a license. He agrees, laughing, and recalls the fourth time he took the test—how it went much like the current drive—until the instructor finally said his driving, while unpleasant, wasn’t technically unsafe. Hazel nods slowly. Gus grins. "Total cancer perk."
A silence settles between them. Then Gus asks, "So what happened to you?" Hazel takes a deep breath.
related_events: Gus's abrupt braking causes Hazel to lurch forward against her seatbelt
Gus accelerates rapidly, causing Hazel's head to snap back
Gus reveals he failed his driving test multiple times
Hazel sarcastically reacts to Gus's driving history
Gus explains his driving was deemed unpleasant but not unsafe
Gus attributes his license approval to being a cancer patient

name: Hazel Tells Gus About Her Diagnosis
description: Gus asks Hazel what happened to her. She takes a deep breath and begins to speak. The car falls silent as she starts to tell him about the time she was thirteen, when they first found the cancer.
related_events: Hazel takes a deep breath before recounting her story
Hazel begins to recount the discovery of her illness

name: Hazel Chooses the Stairs After Seeing a Sick Boy
description: Hazel approaches the elevator as an extremely sick-looking kid holds the door open for her. She hesitates, then decides to take the stairs. The kid nods silently as the elevator doors close. Hazel turns away and begins to walk toward the stairwell.
related_events: Hazel decides to take the stairs instead of the elevator

name: Hazel Collides with Gus and They Share a Moment
description: Hazel turned to leave and walked straight into a tall, lean boy with mahogany hair and blue eyes. 'Ooph. Sorry!' she said. 'No, it's my bad,' he replied. They stood still for a moment, looking at each other without speaking. Hazel said nothing, then murmured, 'Excuse me,' and shuffled away, glancing back as the boy watched her with a faint smile.
related_events: Hazel collides with Gus upon turning away
Hazel and Gus lock eyes after colliding

name: Hazel Leaves in a Hurry After Meeting Gus
description: Hazel breaks eye contact, mutters an excuse, and quickly shuffles away while Gus watches with a faint smile. The elevator doors close behind her as she moves down the hall, disappearing from view.
related_events: Hazel excuses herself and leaves quickly under Gus's gaze

name: Gus Waits, Michael Helps Hazel from the Car
description: Frannie's car pulls up to the house. Michael opens the passenger door and steps out, then helps Hazel out of the car. Gus, who has been sitting on the front stoop, stands up and moves toward them.
related_events: Frannie's car arrives at the house with Hazel returning from the hospital
Michael helps Hazel out of the car

name: Gus and Michael Bond Over a Pacers Jersey
description: Gus stands on the front stoop wearing an Indiana Pacers jersey, holding a bouquet of bright orange tulips. When Frannie's car pulls up, Michael gets out from the passenger side and helps Hazel out of the car. As Gus steps forward to assist, Michael notices the jersey and asks if it’s a Rik Smits jersey. Gus confirms that it is. Michael pauses, then says he loved that player. The two share a quiet moment before Hazel sees Gus and reacts with surprise.
related_events: Gus reveals his Indiana Pacers jersey is a Rik Smits jersey

name: Gus Offers Hazel Tulips and a Picnic Invitation
description: Gus stands on the front stoop holding a bouquet of bright orange tulips. When Frannie's car arrives, he steps forward as Michael helps Hazel out. After exchanging greetings, Gus turns to Hazel and says, 'Hi Hazel.' He pauses, then asks, 'How would you like to go on a picnic?'
related_events: Gus greets Hazel on the front stoop with tulips
Gus invites Hazel on a picnic

name: Gus Learns About Hazel's Disney Wish
description: Gus asks Hazel what she did with her wish. She hesitates, then admits she used it on a trip to Disney World and Epcot Center when she was thirteen. Gus reacts with disbelief, exclaiming that she couldn’t have used her one dying wish on Disney. Hazel looks away, offering a weak defense that they had fun. Gus throws his hands up, calling it the saddest thing he’s ever heard. Hazel mentions she met Goofy, but Gus says he’s now embarrassed. He questions how he can have a crush on a girl with such a cliché wish. Hazel freezes at the word 'crush,' caught off guard. She glances at him, then quickly looks away, blushing. Gus continues talking about Disney, unaware of her reaction, while Hazel remains silent, lost in thought.
related_events: Gus asks Hazel to use her wish
Hazel reveals she used her wish on a trip to Disney World and Epcot Center
Gus reacts with shock and dismay to Hazel's wish
Hazel defends her choice to visit Disney World
Gus expresses embarrassment about Hazel's Disney wish

name: Gus Reveals His Crush on Hazel
description: Gus tells Hazel he has a crush on her. Hazel looks at him, surprised, and then quickly looks away, her face turning red. While Gus keeps talking about Disney, Hazel remains silent, her thoughts fixed on what he just said. She tries not to show how affected she is.
related_events: Gus reveals he has a crush on Hazel
Hazel reacts with surprise and blushes upon hearing about Gus's crush
Hazel becomes preoccupied with the idea of Gus having a crush on her

name: Hazel Makes Her Case for Amsterdam
description: Hazel brings up her recent PET scan results, pointing out how encouraging they are as a reason to travel to Amsterdam. Dr. Maria agrees the results are positive but says they don’t know how long the improvement will last. She shakes her head, saying the trip is out of the question, and explains she’s worried Hazel’s health could worsen in a foreign country. Hazel responds that there are doctors in Amsterdam and that cancer exists everywhere—someone would be able to help if needed. Dr. Maria doesn’t argue the point but says she can’t approve the trip unless someone familiar with Hazel’s condition is there to oversee her care. Hazel immediately turns to her mother, Frannie, and suggests she come along. Frannie looks surprised, but Hazel reminds her she’s never been to Amsterdam and sees from her expression that she’d actually like to go. Dr. Maria glances at Frannie and shrugs, acknowledging the arrangement makes sense. Hazel smiles triumphantly. On that smile, the scene cuts to black. A voice is heard: And then this happened.

Dr. Maria acknowledges the encouraging nature of the PET scan but cautions about its temporary nature
Dr. Maria expresses concern about Hazel's travel due to health risks
Hazel argues for the possibility of traveling to Amsterdam despite health risks

name: Hazel Convinces Dr. Maria with Help from Her Mother
description: Dr. Maria shakes her head, refusing to approve Hazel's trip to Amsterdam unless someone familiar with her medical care accompanies her. Hazel turns to her mother, Frannie, and suggests she come along. Frannie looks surprised but Hazel notices a flicker of interest in her expression. Dr. Maria glances at Frannie and shrugs, conceding that the arrangement makes sense. Hazel smiles triumphantly.

description: Frannie's car pulls up to the back entrance of the Episcopalian sanctuary. Hazel, carrying her oxygen tank, steps out of the car with Frannie's help. She asks if her mother will wait the whole time. Frannie says she won't, claiming she has errands to run, though it's clear she plans to stay nearby. Hazel doesn't challenge her. They tell each other they love one another. As Frannie gets back into the car, she calls out for Hazel to make some friends. Hazel shakes her head and begins to walk toward the entrance.

description: Frannie gets back into the car and calls out to Hazel, telling her to make some friends during the service. Hazel stands by the entrance with her oxygen tank, wearing a blank expression. Without speaking, she slowly shakes her head and turns toward the door.
related_events: Frannie shouts advice to Hazel before getting back in the car
Hazel silently rejects Frannie's advice with a head shake

name: Hazel and Her Mother Visit the Doctor
description: Hazel sits on the edge of an exam table, her legs dangling. An oxygen tube runs beneath her nose. Her mother, Frannie, stands nearby and tells the doctor that Hazel eats very little, rarely leaves the house, and reads the same book over and over. Hazel looks at them and says, "I'm not depressed." The doctor turns to her and says, "She's depressed." Hazel speaks again, louder this time: "I'm not depressed!"

Doctor concludes Hazel is depressed
Hazel repeatedly denies being depressed

name: Hazel in the Mall, Living Room, and Starbucks
description: Hazel walks through a crowded shopping mall with her mother, moving past groups of laughing teenage girls. An oxygen tube runs beneath her nose. Later, she sits on the couch in the living room, watching game shows. Her mother brings her a sandwich, a glass of water, and a handful of prescription pills, which Hazel takes without comment. At a quiet corner of a Starbucks, Hazel reads a worn copy of *An Imperial Affliction*, her eyes fixed on the pages. She looks up briefly as a young couple nearby laughs and plays, then returns to her book.
related_events: Hazel and her mother visit a shopping mall with teenage girls around
Hazel's mother brings her sandwich, water, and medications in the living room
Hazel reads 'An Imperial Affliction' alone at Starbucks

name: Hazel Observes a Playful Couple at Starbucks
description: Hazel sits alone at Starbucks, reading a worn copy of a novel. She glances up as a young man lifts a young woman over his shoulder and spins her around. She watches for a moment, then returns to her book.
related_events: Young man playfully lifts and spins young girl at Starbucks

name: Gus Asks Michael About Her Condition
description: Gus sees Michael walking down the hall and hurries after him. He asks about the woman's condition. Michael tells him she is doing much better. Gus nods, visibly relieved.
related_events: Gus races after Michael to ask about her condition
Michael reassures Gus that she is doing much better

name: Gus Asks Michael to Pass on a Message
description: Gus waits in the hallway, his foot tapping nervously. When he sees Michael walking down the hall, he rushes over and asks about her condition. Michael replies that she is doing much better. Gus nods, visibly relieved, and says the staff won’t allow him to visit because only family is permitted. He asks Michael to let her know he was there. Michael assures him he will. Gus smiles, thanks him, and sits back down. Michael looks at him with kindness and suggests he go home and rest. Gus looks up, considering it, then stays in his seat.
related_events: Gus requests Michael to convey his presence to her
Michael promises to deliver Gus's message

name: Michael Suggests Rest and Gus Agrees
description: Michael notices Gus sitting with his foot tapping, looking tired. He tells Gus to go home and get some rest. Gus looks up, considers the suggestion, then nods in agreement. He stands and leaves, heading home.
related_events: Michael suggests Gus go home and rest
Gus accepts Michael's suggestion to go home

name: Gus Waits Outside
description: Gus paces nervously, then takes a seat near the entrance, unable to see her because only family is allowed inside. Michael approaches, and Gus asks about her condition. After learning she is doing much better, Gus expresses relief and asks Michael to let her know he was there. Michael agrees, and Gus remains seated, choosing to stay nearby even though he does not go in.
related_events: Gus decides to remain nearby despite not being allowed to visit

name: Gus and Michael Talk About Survival
description: Frannie offers Gus a drink, but he declines, saying he's fine. Michael sits beside Gus on the stairs and asks if he’s a survivor too. Gus taps his leg and says he didn’t cut it off for the hell of it, though it would be a good weight-loss strategy—legs are heavy. Michael asks how his health is now. Gus says he’s been N-E-C for fourteen months. Michael calls that fantastic. Gus says he’s very lucky.

Michael asks Gus about his survival experience
Gus reveals leg amputation and sobriety duration

name: Michael Warns Gus About Hazel's Health
description: Michael sits with Gus downstairs and tells him that Hazel is still very sick and always will be, explaining that her lungs are weak even if she tries to keep up. As he speaks, Hazel, upstairs, stops what she is doing and listens. She hears her father talking about her condition. A moment later, she calls down, asking Gus if he is ready, and appears, interrupting the conversation.

Hazel overhears conversation about her health

name: Hazel Interrupts the Conversation
description: Upstairs, Hazel finishes getting ready for her date. She places orange flowers in a toothbrush holder and puts on lip gloss. Standing in front of the mirror, she studies her reflection and continues her preparations. From downstairs, she hears her father speaking. Hazel interrupts Michael to ask Gus if he is ready

Her phone buzzes in her lap, and she glances down to see a message from Gus: 'Tell me my copy is missing the last ten pages or something.' Her eyes widen in surprise, and a small smile appears on her lips. She looks back up, straightens her expression, and resumes eating as if nothing happened.

Hazel reacts to Gus's message with a smile

name: Hazel Reacts to Gus's Second Message While Parents Exchange a Glance
description: Hazel receives a text from Gus asking if he has truly reached the end of the book. She smiles, unable to suppress her amusement. At the table, her parents, Frannie and Michael, exchange a knowing glance.

Frannie and Michael exchange a knowing glance

name: Hazel Laughs at Gus's Text and Michael Intervenes
description: Hazel reads a third message from Gus, this one filled with exaggerated outrage over a book ending mid-sentence. She bursts out laughing, unable to contain her amusement. Michael clears his throat and looks at her, then asks if she would like to be excused from the table.

Hazel laughs out loud at Gus's message

description: Hazel sits in bed reading Gus's novella when Frannie appears in the doorway, noticing the book. Frannie comments that it's different, and Hazel shrugs. Frannie asks if Gus gave it to her. Hazel responds by joking about herpes, and Frannie rolls her eyes. Hazel's phone buzzes. She picks it up quickly, her expression brightening, then falling. Frannie sees the change and says, "I'm sure he'll call, don't worry." Hazel insists she isn't worried, that it's no big deal—they just hung out. Frannie doesn't respond, only looks at her. Hazel rolls her eyes. In the following days, Hazel brushes her teeth, watches TV, eats breakfast, and stares out the window on a rainy afternoon, each time glancing at her phone, waiting.

name: Hazel Checks Her Phone Again and Again
description: Hazel brushes her teeth, pausing to glance at her phone. Later, she sits on the couch watching TV, her hand reaching for the phone, unlocking it, then setting it down. At the kitchen table, she eats breakfast between glances at the screen. Outside, rain streaks the window. She stands by it, staring out, arms crossed, then turns away, resists, and finally picks up her phone once more. She doesn't say anything, but her face tightens with frustration.
related_events: Hazel brushes her teeth while checking her phone
Hazel watches TV while checking her phone
Hazel eats breakfast while checking her phone
Hazel looks out the window on a rainy day, resisting then checking her phone

name: Hazel Wakes Up and Sees Her Parents
description: Hazel opens her eyes to the steady beep of a heart monitor. A nurse stands nearby and tells her she’s going to be okay. Hazel whispers a quiet response, then nods when the nurse asks if she wants to see her parents. The nurse leaves and returns with Hazel’s mother and father. They rush to her bedside, crying, kissing her face and holding her. Later, Hazel lies in bed as her parents explain what happened. name: Hazel Writes to Van Houten and Reads the Letter to Gus
description: Hazel sits at her computer and begins typing an email to Peter Van Houten. She introduces herself as Hazel Grace Lancaster and mentions that her friend Augustus Waters read Van Houten’s book at her recommendation. She explains that Augustus received an email from Van Houten and shared it with her, and she hopes it’s not a bother that she’s writing. She lists her questions about what happens after the end of the novel—whether Anna’s mother marries the Dutch Tulip Man, whether he is up to something or simply misunderstood, what becomes of Anna’s friends, and what happens to Sisyphus the Hamster. She says these questions have haunted her for years and she would like answers while she still can. She adds that she would love to read anything else Van Houten writes, even his grocery lists, and signs the letter with her name and age. Later, she reads the letter aloud to Augustus over the phone. When she finishes, Augustus says, 'Not bad.' Hazel asks if he thinks it’s good. He says it’s a bit pretentious, but Van Houten uses words like 'tendentious' and 'bacchanalia,' so he’ll probably like it. Hazel smiles, notices the time, and says she needs to go to sleep. Augustus says okay, and Hazel says okay back. Neither hangs up. They laugh, and Augustus suggests that 'ok' could be their 'always.' Hazel says 'ok,' and so does Augustus, twice more. Then he hangs up. Hazel stays on her bed, looking at the phone, thinking.

name: Hazel and Her Parents Receive Treatment Update from Oncology Team
description: Hazel sits at a large conference table with her parents and her oncology team, including Dr. Maria and three other doctors. An oncologist begins by saying that Phalanxifor is still controlling the growth of her tumor, but there are ongoing issues with fluid buildup in her body. The room falls silent when the doctor asks how they should proceed. Hazel looks around, waiting for someone to respond, then says she doesn’t feel qualified to answer. The doctor clarifies he was speaking to Dr. Simmons, an older man with a white beard. Dr. Simmons explains that the tumors haven’t become resistant to the treatment, which is unusual, but the drug might be making the fluid problem worse. Dr. Maria adds that stopping the medication could lead to more serious risks. Michael, Hazel’s father, asks if they are just going to do nothing. Dr. Maria says they need to decide together, noting that few patients have been on Phalanxifor as long as Hazel, so the long-term effects are unknown. Hazel asks if she could get a lung transplant. The doctors exchange glances until Dr. Maria tells her she wouldn’t be considered a strong candidate. Hazel nods, trying to appear unaffected, but Michael begins to cry and reaches for his wife Frannie’s hand. Dr. Simmons starts explaining the medical challenges in technical terms, but Hazel stops listening, her eyes fixed on her parents as they hold hands and struggle to keep their emotions hidden.

name: Hazel Sends Goodbye Texts to Augustus
description: Hazel reads from 'An Imperial Affliction' when her phone buzzes with a message from Augustus. He writes 'hello?' and then, 'The silence is deafening.' She puts the phone down, her heart breaking, but after a moment picks it up again. She texts him, 'I don't know if you'll understand this but I can't see you anymore. I mean I want to. I just...' Then she adds, 'I'm a grenade,' and sends it. After a pause, she sends another message: 'When I look at you, all I can see is what I'm going to put you through. I can't have that. I'm sorry.' She waits. Augustus replies with 'Ok.' Hazel responds with 'Ok.' A moment later, he writes, 'oh my god, stop flirting with me!' She explains that eventually, no one will remember Cleopatra, Mozart, or Muhammad Ali, and certainly no one will remember them. She says oblivion is inevitable, and if that scares someone, the only thing to do is ignore it, like everyone else does. name: Hazel Awakens from a Memory and Rejoins the Meeting

'I have a question.' Dr. Maria turned to her. 'Yes, Hazel.' Hazel took a breath. 'Can I still go to Amsterdam?' Dr. Simmons let out a short laugh. The room went still. He cleared his throat. 'That would not be wise at this juncture.' 'Why not?' Hazel asked. He hesitated. Dr. Maria stepped in. 'It would... increase some risks.' 'So does going to the mall,' Hazel said. 'Yes, but an airplane?' Dr. Maria replied. 'They have oxygen on airplanes,' Hazel said. Frannie said her name gently. 'It's my life, right?' Hazel looked around the table. 'I have this opportunity I may never have again. If the medicine's working, I don't see why—' Dr. Simmons cut in. 'Because, Hazel.' He paused. 'Look, I don't know any other way to say this... You're just too sick.' The words landed heavily. He added, 'I'm sorry.' No one spoke. The weight of the moment settled over them all.

name: Hazel Asks About Amsterdam
description: Hazel interrupts the meeting to ask Dr. Maria if she can still go to Amsterdam. Dr. Simmons laughs, drawing looks from everyone in the room. He clears his throat.
